author: YugShah1510
title: iGPU Tests (unit) / GPU fails - no supported GPU devices found on runner
signature: Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed: [GPU] Can't get <PROPERTY> property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU Tests (unit) / GPU
failed_jobs.symptom: benchmark_app sample fails to load model to GPU device because no OpenCL platforms are visible on the runner

key_errors:
[ ERROR ] Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:117:
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:112:
Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed at src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593:
[GPU] Can't get PERFORMANCE_HINT property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query.
[GPU] Please check OpenVINO documentation for GPU drivers setup guide.
root_cause: The `clinfo` step run just before benchmark_app reports 'Number of platforms  0', meaning the OpenCL ICD cannot see any GPU devices on this self-hosted iGPU runner. This causes the intel_gpu plugin's device enumeration (`!m_device_map.empty()` check in plugin.cpp:593) to fail immediately when benchmark_app tries to load the model with '-d GPU'. This is not a code regression from the merged PR (#38633, unrelated Node.js Buffer handling change) - it is the same recurring runner/driver-level failure recorded 4 times previously since 2026-10-20, now occurring a 5th time, indicating the iGPU self-hosted runner pool has an intermittent or persistent GPU driver/device exposure problem (missing OpenCL ICD registration, container not passing through /dev/dri, or driver crash) rather than a software defect in OpenVINO.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires access to the specific self-hosted iGPU runner. To diagnose: on the affected runner (or container), run `clinfo` and confirm 'Number of platforms' is 0; check /dev/dri device nodes are present and passed into the container, check that the intel-opencl-icd / intel-level-zero-gpu packages and kernel i915 driver are correctly installed and loaded, and check for recent driver/container image changes.
recommended_actions: Escalate to CI infrastructure team: this iGPU runner pool has failed devices-query 5 times since 2026-10-20 - treat as a known recurring infra issue, not a code bug.
On the affected runner/container image, verify /dev/dri/* nodes exist and are passed through, and that 'clinfo' lists at least one GPU platform before the job starts.
Add a pre-flight 'clinfo' platform-count check (fail fast with a clear infra error) to iGPU test jobs so future occurrences are immediately distinguishable from code regressions.
Consider temporarily excluding/quarantining the affected runner from the iGPU test pool until the OpenCL/driver setup is repaired.
prevention_strategies: Add a runner health-check step (e.g., `clinfo` platform count > 0) that fails fast with an explicit 'runner GPU unavailable' message before launching benchmark_app/test suites, so infra failures are not conflated with code regressions. Track iGPU runner health via periodic smoke tests outside of post-commit CI.
historical_context: Identical signature recorded 4 times previously in the pattern database (first seen 2026-10-20T09:11:02Z, most recently 2026-10-20T21:22:20Z) across different commits/PRs unrelated to GPU code, confirming this is a persistent runner-level infrastructure problem rather than a code-induced regression. This run is the 5th occurrence.
